_comment: Fragment 46 — D-93: the missing critic. Phase closure, the return path, and the first proof-of-concept. Merged 2026-08-21.

nodes.label: D-93 — The Missing Critic: Phase Closure and the Judge
nodes.description: The development lane model had three proposers and no critic. Lane A wrote the specs, wrote the checks that verify the specs, and judged whether its own output passed. D-93 adds a Critic role held by Lane A on a separate turn, and a Judge role held by the user at phase boundaries only.
nodes.rationale: D-82 recorded that D-75 cannot enforce itself and it was never closed, because no check can close it. Every control installed since detects shape, never judgment. The gap needed a role, not another control.

nodes.label: The Critic Is a Role, Not a Fourth Agent
nodes.description: A fourth agent was considered and rejected. It would add a fourth surface, a fourth set of crossing boundaries and a fourth phase. The cost of role-instead-of-agent is stated rather than hidden: the critic shares the proposer's blind spots.
nodes.rationale: The proposal named this as its own first risk, the cure becoming the disease. Three mitigations carry the weight instead: the separate turn, the reject budget, and a Judge who is someone else entirely.

nodes.label: Four Conditions Close a Phase, Not Three
nodes.description: Artifacts exist, every handoff entry has reached a terminal disposition, a critic pass is recorded, and the Judge approves. Condition two deliberately raises the bar that check 10 sets during a phase.
nodes.rationale: D-19 gave sprints an artifact Definition of Done and phases never got one, so a phase ended when Lane A said it ended. That is G32's shape one level up. Acknowledging is not answering, and a phase boundary is precisely where that distinction is supposed to bite.

nodes.label: A Critic Pass That Never Rejects Is Not a Critic Pass
nodes.description: The critic pass runs on a separate turn, reads the artifacts rather than its own summary of them, records findings even when already fixed, and reports zero findings as a finding in itself. The reject count, not the pass rate, is the health metric.
nodes.rationale: A pass appended to the work being criticised is the author checking their own summary, which is the summary-outlived-source failure. A pass that always approves is a check that cannot fail wearing a different hat.

nodes.label: Phases Run Forward and Findings Do Not
nodes.description: A Phase 2 finding can require Lane A work in a phase already closed. One template field records it and the phase register row is marked Reopened, citing the entry. A reopened phase is not a failure.
nodes.rationale: Until this existed the only options were an undeclared reopening or a dropped finding. A phase never reopened across a whole build more likely means findings were dropped than that none existed.

nodes.label: Lane B Exercised the Channel Before Writing Any Code
nodes.description: Lane B started Phase 2 and filed three handoff entries before the first line of application code existed. All three were defects in Lane A's own output, and all three stand: a register contradiction, an authoritative config file shipped incomplete, and a dependency whose consumers were removed while the dependency stayed.
nodes.rationale: The ordering is the evidence. The feedback channel proved itself before the code it was built to support existed, which is the strongest available demonstration that D-90 and D-92 built the right thing.

nodes.label: Every Check Verifies Arrival and None Verifies Correctness
nodes.description: Lane A shipped three defects into a phase it was about to declare complete and its own checks caught none of them. A claim reaching a tier, a file existing, a hash matching — all are arrival. G65 recorded this limit for one check; it is a property of the whole apparatus.
nodes.rationale: Stating it is the honest disposition rather than a defect to fix. It is also the argument for the critic role: the thing no check can do is judge whether what arrived is right.
